He undergoes stress testing, which reproduces his symptoms and reveals signs of inducible ischemia
To reduce his anginal episodes, his physician initiates a medication that improves oxygen delivery to the myocardium primarily through vascular smooth muscle relaxation.
Within minutes of taking the medication sublingually during an episode of chest pain, the patient reports symptom relief.
The drug does not affect cardiac contractility or significantly dilate coronary arteries at lower doses.
Instead, it works by reducing myocardial oxygen demand by decreasing preload.
The patient is advised to sit down before taking the medication to avoid dizziness.
On follow-up, the frequency of anginal episodes has declined, and the patient tolerates the treatment well.
He is instructed not to take the medication with phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors.
The prescribing physician explains that the agent functions by activating an intracellular signaling cascade that leads to dephosphorylation of myosin light chains in vascular smooth muscle.

encounters.cc: Evaluation of a chronic wound on the bottom of his right foot first noticed three weeks ago

lines: Evaluation of a chronic wound on the bottom of his right foot first noticed three weeks ago
The patient is a 66-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus with peripheral neuropathy and coronary artery disease who presents for evaluation of a chronic wound on his right foot.
He has established longitudinal care in internal medicine and cardiology, most recently evaluated one year prior for stable angina.
He reports first noticing the lesion approximately three weeks ago when his wife pointed out blood on his sock, although he himself had not felt any pain.
He reports that for the past few years, he has had a "tingly" or "numb" feeling in both feet, especially at night when lying in bed.
Occasionally, this sensation disrupts his sleep.
He denies fever, chills, or drainage from the wound.
The lesion does not interfere with his ability to walk, but he mentions that over the last few months, he has had difficulty feeling the gas pedal while driving.
He has no back pain or radiating leg symptoms.

encounters.cc: Three-day history of sudden sharp pain in the back of his right ankle with clicking sensation and inability to bear weight

lines: Three-day history of sudden sharp pain in the back of his right ankle with clicking sensation and inability to bear weight

The patient is a 70-year-old male with coronary artery disease, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, type 2 diabetes mellitus with peripheral neuropathy, and major depressive disorder who presents to the Emergency Department.

He follows with Psychiatry for management of depressive symptoms following his recent hospitalization for acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction and has a history of right foot complications previously evaluated in Podiatry.
He describes a sharp, stabbing pain that began while walking down a flight of stairs and reports worsening with any movement.
He denies trauma, fever, or swelling elsewhere.
He reports difficulty bearing weight on the right foot and notes a "clicking" sensation near the heel.
He also reports that his mood has worsened significantly over the past month.

He describes feeling increasingly fatigued, has lost interest in his usual routines, and is no longer regularly attending his community senior center, which he attributes to his mother's recent diagnosis of metastatic small cell lung carcinoma, leaving him feeling "helpless and guilty." He denies suicidal ideation but reports sleeping more during the day and skipping meals.
He recently requested refills for all of his medications during a telehealth check-in but failed to mention his ankle symptoms at that time.
He expresses worry that the added stress may be affecting his sleep and appetite and acknowledges being less consistent with his medications lately.
